title: Retail Sales Performance Report: 2023–2024
executive_summary: Across 508 orders, the business generated $441,146 in total revenue over the 2023–2024 period, with a healthy 9.9% year-over-year increase from 2023 to 2024. The East region led all regions in revenue. A data issue prevented quarterly 2024 breakdowns from being computed. High-discount Electronics orders represent a notable revenue concentration, and the overall order revenue distribution is highly skewed, signalling a wide mix of order sizes.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 508 orders generating total revenue of $441,146. The average order value is $868.40, though this figure is heavily influenced by large outlier orders (see q6).
The East region produced the highest revenue at $128,297, followed closely by North at $124,324, then West at $98,835, and South at $89,690. The East–South gap is approximately $38,607.

Quarterly revenue figures for all four quarters of 2024 (Q1–Q4) returned $0.00, indicating that the analysis pipeline could not assign 2024 orders to calendar quarters. This is likely a consequence of date-parsing failures in the cleaning stage and should be treated as unreliable.
Revenue grew from $210,206 in 2023 to $230,940 in 2024, a year-over-year increase of approximately 9.9%. This represents an absolute gain of roughly $20,733.

22 Electronics orders carried a discount of 20% or more, generating $50,035 in combined revenue. These high-discount orders account for approximately 11.3% of total revenue, suggesting meaningful margin exposure in this category.

Order revenue ranges from $5.27 to $7,844.02. The mean order value is $868.40 but the median is only $315.76, confirming a right-skewed distribution driven by a small number of very large orders. The standard deviation of $1,307.86 further reflects this high variability.

There are 222 unique customers. The single highest-revenue customer contributed $14,279, representing 3.2% of total revenue. This low concentration suggests the business is not overly dependent on any one customer.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; all findings should be interpreted with caution until root causes are resolved.
The 2024 quarterly revenue figures (Q1–Q4) are all $0.00, almost certainly due to date-parsing errors in the cleaning stage. No quarterly trend analysis is possible from this run.
The year-over-year and quarterly figures depend on correct date assignment; if dates were partially mis-parsed, the 2023/2024 split may also be inaccurate.
The dataset covers only 508 orders, which may not be a complete export of all transactions for the period, limiting the representativeness of the findings.
No product-level or margin data is available, so revenue figures cannot be translated into profitability conclusions.
conclusion: Despite pipeline validation failures, the available data indicates solid overall performance: $441,146 in revenue across 508 orders and a ~9.9% year-over-year revenue increase. The East and North regions are the strongest contributors. High-discount Electronics orders warrant margin scrutiny, and the highly skewed order distribution suggests a long tail of small transactions alongside a few very large ones. Customer concentration is low. The critical priority before the next reporting cycle is resolving the date-parsing failures so that quarterly trends can be accurately computed and all findings fully validated.
